ORDINAL MARKUP
Cross-tree purchases only. Reset-triggering upgrades, exclusive choices, and chamber-consuming Reversal builds are left manual. Full autonomous Reality/Fabric progression is not implemented in this patch.

Actions

Tutorial

Everything in the game, from your first click to the New Era, Boosters, Challenges and Incrementy. Open a section to read it.

1. Ordinals: the basics

The big number at the top is Hα(base): a Hardy-hierarchy value, where α is your ordinal and the number in brackets is your base (10 at the start). You do not play with the number directly; you grow the ordinal and the number follows.

  • Increase Ordinal by 1 (I) adds 1 to the finite part of your ordinal. The number grows.
  • Maximize ordinal (O) turns a finite part that has reached the base into the next limit step (for example +10 becomes ω in base 10). The number does not increase, but your ordinal gets far stronger, so the next Increases are worth much more. Anything above the base is lost, so Maximize as soon as you reach it.
  • The bottom bar is linear: it shows how close you are to the next Markup (orange), in the New Era to your next Factor Boost (blue), and inside a Challenge to your next Challenge goal (green), with the time you still need at your current speed.
2. How ordinals work (the carry rule)

Ordinals here are written like numbers in your current base. Every coefficient must stay below the base. When a coefficient reaches the base it carries into the next exponent: in base 4, ω·4 becomes ω2; ω2·3+ω·3+4 becomes ω3. Exponents follow the same rule, so ωω+4 becomes ωω2 (base 4). Terms are always written from highest to lowest.

A lower base means carries happen sooner, so you climb the ordinal ladder much faster. That is why Factor Shifts (which lower the base) are so powerful. The first ladder is ω, ω·2, …, ω2, ω3, …, ωω, and so on. In base 3 the limit of this system is ωωω, which is where the New Era begins.

3. Markup and Ordinal Points (OP)

When your number reaches the Markup threshold (base × 2base, which is 10,240 at base 10) you can Markup (K). A Markup resets your ordinal and gives Ordinal Points (OP). Every succession counts: each rung of ω you have maximized plus each unmaxed Increase (your first Markup gives about 100 OP). If you leave more than one base worth of Increases unmaxed, the surplus is square-rooted for every 10 successions, so Maximize regularly. OP is the currency for almost everything in the Markup panel.

  • Markups reset your ordinal but do not reset Tier 1 automation or Factors. Your automation levels and Factor levels are preserved before and after the New Era.
  • Quadrupler (Markup panel, costs 1,000 OP): ×4 OP from Markups for the current run.
  • Booster upgrades can multiply Markup OP (×5, and ×666,666 at a base below 6).
  • In the New Era your OP is not spent freely: it always equals your ordinal (your count of successions).
4. Factors

Factors multiply your Tier 1 automation by (level + 1) each. You start with Factor 1 (cost 10 OP). Each further Factor is unlocked by a Factor Shift, and its base cost is the previous one squared (10, 100, 104, 108, …). Every level you buy squares that Factor's price, so each Factor can only be bought a handful of times. Prices have no ceiling: they are OmegaNums. Max Factors buys as many as you can afford, cheapest first.

5. Factor Shifts (lowering the base)

There are 7 Factor Shifts. Each lowers your base by 1 (10 → 3), unlocks the next Factor, and resets your current ordinal and Tier 1 automation (OP and Factors are kept). Costs: 1,000 / 8,000 / 50,000 / 750,000 / 1e13 / 1e22 / 2.122e101 OP. At base 5 you unlock the Dynamic Factor.

Dynamic Factor: starts at 1 and grows over time up to its cap (10 at first). It multiplies every Factor by its square root and all automation by its full value. Manifolds (see Incrementy) raise the cap and make it grow \u00D71.1 faster each (at most \u00D7900).

6. Tier 1 automation (Autoclickers)

Two autoclickers press your Ordinals buttons for you: Auto Increase (presses Increase) and Auto Maximize (presses Maximize). Each level presses once per second, multiplied by all your Factors, the Dynamic Factor and other bonuses. Both start at 100 OP and double in price each purchase. Max All (M) spends your OP on Factors first (half your OP), then on the two autoclickers (80% Increase / 20% Maximize). You also start every Factor Boost with a free Maximize autoclicker.

7. Tier 2 automation and Auto Markup

Booster upgrades unlock two Tier 2 autoclickers: Max All and Markup. They press once per second, boosted by challenge rewards and Incrementy (they can no longer be upgraded with OP). Toggle them on the Boosters panel, Autobuyers tab, where their clicks per second are shown. Buying a Booster upgrade also buys the cheaper ones above it in its column if you can afford all of them.

  • Auto Markup always works inside the New Era, where Markup + Max All is how you gain successions.
  • Outside the New Era choose a mode: New Era only (off), When a Markup gives at least X OP, or Every X seconds (both need the Markup threshold reached).
8. The New Era (ψ(Ω))

In base 3, when your ordinal reaches ωωω it becomes ψ(Ω) and stops growing the normal way. Now one Markup (I) followed by one Max All (M) is exactly 1 succession of your new ordinal. Your OP and your Tier 1 autoclickers both equal your ordinal, and Factor Boosts need a number of successions to be reached. The new ordinal is written in capital Ω notation from highest to lowest term and uses lowercase ω only for the smallest steps. The limit of the era is the Bachmann–Howard ordinal, ψ(Ω2).

The Tier 2 autoclickers (Markup + Max All) do these presses for you.

9. Factor Boosts

The Factor Boost button sits right under the Markup button on the Ordinals tab. It shows how many Boosters it gives, the exact ordinal you need, how close you are (%), and roughly how long it will take at your current speed. The n-th Factor Boost gives n Boosters; if you qualify for several at once, one click does them all (bulk) unless you switch Bulk Factor Boosts off in the Options, then every Factor Boost is exactly 1. A Factor Boost resets your run (ordinal, OP, Factors, shifts, automation) but keeps all Boosters, Booster upgrades, challenge progress and Tier 2 settings.

Factor Boosts #1 to #24 need 109, 324, 972, 8,748, 26,244, ... up to 2.001e17 successions. Boost #25 and every later one targets BHO, ψ(Ω2), at 4.863e19 successions. Between the 24th target and BHO your ordinal passes through 4 extra stages (ΩΩ22+Ω2+ω, ΩΩ22+Ωω, ΩΩ2ω and ΩΩω) that are not Boost targets.

10. Boosters and Booster upgrades

Boosters are spent on the left three columns of the Boosters panel. Refunding (R) gives them all back but resets your Factor Shifts (you can toggle a confirmation, and whether to Factor Boost at the same time).

  • Factors ×2 (1) • Max All autoclicker (1) • Markup autoclicker (1)
  • ×5 OP (5) • Unspent Boosters boost Tier 1 and 2 automation by ×(10 + unspent Boosters) (4) • 20 OP per second (8)
  • Base −4 if over 7 (72, resets your ordinal) • Base always five below ψ(Ω) (73) • 3 free Factors each (16)
  • Dynamic squared in odd challenges (53) • Dynamic decreases much slower (74) • ×666,666 OP below base 6 (66)

The right column is milestones on total Boosters earned (nothing is spent): 12 unlocks Challenges, 28 unlocks Incrementy, 108 extends Incrementy, 324 is the next layer (no effect yet).

11. Challenges

Unlocked at 12 total Boosters. Entering resets your run (like a Factor Boost without Boosters). Each challenge has 3 goals; reaching a goal completes it and gives a permanent multiplier to Tier 1 and Tier 2 automation. Exit whenever you like.

  • 1 Bottleneck: Tier 1 autoclickers capped at level 1, Dynamic gain halved.
  • 2 No Factors: Factors cannot be bought; Challenge 1's reward is negated. Challenges 1 and 2 suppress each other's reward while active.
  • 3 Higher Base: the starting base is 15. • 4 Fixed Base: Factor Shifts do not lower the base. • 5 Two Shifts: at most 2 Factor Shifts.
  • 6 Fading: Dynamic Factor collapses, Quadrupler disabled, OP resets every Markup, no Booster upgrades, 1000 manual Increase clicks per Markup.
  • 7 Everything: Challenges 1–6 all at once. • 8 Refunded: all upgrades refunded, Decrementy divides Tier 1, no challenge rewards, repeatable.
12. Incrementy, Manifolds and Decrementy

After your first Collapse every earlier feature stays unlocked (Boosters, Markup, Challenges, Incrementy and its extensions, both Tier 2 autoclickers). Incrementy is unlocked at 28 total Boosters and only produced in the New Era. Incrementy boosts Tier 2 automation and buys rebuyable upgrades (Incrementy multiplier to the 1.02: 300 ×30 per level, doubled production: 30 ×10, ×1.2: 1e4 ×300) and, from 108 Boosters, six one-time extensions (2e6 up to 5e11). Manifolds cost 1e3^n Incrementy (doubling growth) plus n Dynamic Factor and each raises the Dynamic Factor cap. Decrementy only exists in Challenge 8, where it divides your Tier 1 automation.

Collapse, Cardinals and Aleph upgrades

Once you are at BHO (with the last Booster upgrade for your first Collapse) you can Collapse: a bigger reset that gives Cardinals. Split Cardinals into the three Aleph types, combine them into ℵω, and spend them on Aleph and Dark upgrades. After the first Collapse every earlier feature stays unlocked. Singularity Function SFU111 adds 8 more Aleph upgrades (AU17-AU24) and 16 more (AU25-AU40, each costing factorially more than the last), and AU17 makes ℵ2's OP multiplier also give that much OP per second.

Details: Cardinals are divided between ℵ0, ℵ1 and ℵ2, and each type has an amount and a power. The smallest of the three can be turned into ℵω, which pays for upgrades. Challenge 8 (Decrementy) has uncapped ordinals and increasingly demanding repeatable goals; Decrementy produces Dark Manifolds, which raise your Singularity Level and unlock Dark upgrades. Sluggish and Baseless milestones come from Collapsing repeatedly.

Omega Challenges

Special challenges with very large goals. Every completion is measured on a log scale (reaching the goal once is 1 completion, double the exponent is 2) and gives multipliers to OP and Booster gain. Several later features add to them: Super and Godly particles add a flat bonus to each Omega Challenge, and Universe fragment gain counts your completions.

Singularity and Singularity Functions

The Singularity is a layer above Collapse. Each Singularity Level (SL) needs 3× more successions than the one before, and the ordinal shown at that exact point is the SL's ordinal. SL is raised with Dark Manifolds, Manifolds and Incrementy and gives Singularity Functions to spend on SFU upgrades, plus Refund Points. SFU111 unlocks 8 Aleph upgrades. SFU120 (needs SL300, every non-Universal achievement and every earlier SFU) unlocks the Universe.

Details: you can raise your SL three ways: spend Dark Manifolds, reach more Manifolds, or spend Incrementy. Each SL gives one Singularity Function; Refund Points let you take SFUs back. Super particles lower every Boost target, so every ordinal stage comes earlier, but the SL's ordinal is always shown exactly when its requirement is reached.

Tiers: tier 1 is SL1, where the New Era runs from Ω to BHO; every later block of about 40 Singularity Levels is another tier. In tier 2 each succession is worth one whole BHO of tier 1 and the tier's own BHO is 4.863e19× further away, and so on for every tier. Counts are kept in tier units, so they never overflow however high your SL gets, and reaching a tier's BHO moves you into the next tier.

The Universe, fragments and particles

The Universe tab holds a reset that wipes EVERYTHING (only options, achievements and Universe progress stay) for Universal Fragments. It needs SL350. You get exactly 1 until your Singularity Level and your ordinal both pass 350; after that it grows very slowly with SL, ordinal and Omega Challenge completions. Fragments multiply ordinal gain and each fragment emits a particle about every 30 s that you click to catch (they never spawn on top of the ordinal or buttons).

  • 10 rarities, each factorially rarer: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythical, Divine, Super, Omega, Godly. Every particle adds a little OP gain and Refund Points over time, and each rarity has its own bonuses (Common: Tier 1 and Markup requirement, Super: Boost requirement /(1 + 1% per particle) so every ordinal stage comes earlier, Omega unlocks 10 Booster upgrades, Godly exponentiates OP, Tier 1 and Booster gain).
  • You can turn particles and the magnet off in Options → Gameplay.

Details: the Orbit upgrade makes two particles circle the ordinal; they earn EXP from your ordinal amount (^1.5 in the New Era), level up to 5^Rarity times and each level needs 1.25× more EXP. Other upgrades make particles come to you, collect themselves and be worth more.

Universe upgrades

Spend fragments in the Universe tab: Particle Magnet (3 levels: auto-collect and pull toward your cursor), Stable Universe (rarer particles 2× likelier), Particle Orbit (2 particles orbit the ordinal, level up with EXP from your ordinal and boost it by rarity), Diversity, Particle Amplifier, Automation, Glyphs, Passive Tier 1 and Reversal, plus 25 more spread through the tree: Sieves that divide the spawn chance of particles (and glyphs) so rarer ones come more often, and upgrades that strengthen the Reversal. The tree can be collapsed with the button above it.

Automation tab

Automate Singularity, Decrementy, FB/s, passive Boosters, Cardinals / Collapse and Omega Challenges. Each automation costs fragments and particles. Autoprestigers and Tier 2 automation also move here.

The six automations: Singularity (Dark Manifolds, Manifolds and Incrementy), Decrementy (cycles Challenge 8), FB/s (stop at a chosen Factor Boost count), Passive Booster gain, Cardinals and Collapse (distribute, buy ℵω and upgrades, Collapse) and Omega Challenges (cycle the ones you pick). Entering and leaving challenges by automation resets your run exactly like doing it by hand.

Glyphs

Every 10 Challenge 8 completions you find a glyph (Common 60%, Uncommon 30%, Rare 10%). Equip one: Common raises OP gain to a power, Uncommon multiplies every Factor, Rare multiplies Booster gain and FB/s. The equipped glyph orbits the ordinal.

Reversal and Space Waves

Sacrifice fragments to build Spatial Chambers that make Space Waves. Waves boost the Singularity, divide its successions, boost Incrementy (also per Singularity Level) and multiply Factors. Reversal upgrades (Graviton, Particle Manipulation, Particle Containment, Nuclear Acceleration and 10 more further right in the tree) are bought with fragments or Space Waves; each of the 10 new ones costs (n+1) times the one before.

Details: each Spatial Chamber makes √size/100 Space Waves per second. Waves can be spent on upgrades that speed up the game, boost the Singularity, divide its successions and boost Incrementy per Singularity Level.

13. Achievements

Achievements unlock automatically. The bar at the top shows how many you have. The Universal achievements (u1-u22) are not needed for SFU120.

14. Hotkeys and options

I increase • O maximize • M Max All • K markup • S Factor Shift • R refund (Boosters panel) • Esc closes panels. Options let you change ordinal notation (100 styles), number precision, ordinal length, colours, fonts and tickspeed. Save and export/import saves in Options → Data.

Fabric (the ultimate reset)

Once Reality is unlocked, the Fabric tab shows a very demanding list of stats. When every one is met you can reset everything below Fabric for permanent Space Fabric. The reward is a geometric mean of how far each stat is past its threshold (no stat counts for more than 4x your weakest), so it rewards balanced progress.

  • Space Fabric makes your Singularity Level grow passively: you gain 10^sx levels per second and the exponent sx itself grows exponentially (a small percentage per second set by Space Fabric and its upgrades), up to a raised cap. There is no floor. The title shows the post-New Era ordinal of your Singularity Level and nothing else.
  • It multiplies Incrementy, Tier 1 / Tier 2 automation and OP, and grants Incrementy on every reset.
  • It runs Tier 2 automation at its best setting and the Autoprestigers at full speed; milestones add Universe Automation, particle collection and passive fragments / Space Waves.
  • Fabric Essence is a separate, permanent resource produced passively (√(1+Space Fabric) × (1+log10(1+total Space Fabric)) per second). It survives every reset. Each of five thresholds (1e3, 1e6, 1e12, 1e24, 1e48) raises the Essence Tower by one: passive Incrementy is multiplied by the genuine tetration 2↑↑height (2, 4, 16, 65536, 2^65536), and Essence also scales Singularity growth by a logarithmic factor.
  • The whole original game moves to the Old Features tab and keeps working.

Effects

Universe particle options appear once the Universe is unlocked. For a global switch that turns glows, shadows and animations off, use Low-lag mode under Performance.

Refresh rate

How often the game updates. Lower = smoother (and uses more CPU). It does not change game speed.

Low-lag mode

Keeps the game smooth when ordinals or numbers get huge (drawing only; production is untouched).
What does Low-lag mode change?
Low-lag / Optimize mode keeps the game smooth when ordinals or numbers get huge. While it is ON: (1) Singularity ordinals are cut to at most 40 visible characters, and that limit shrinks by itself (down to 12) whenever drawing a frame takes longer than 40 ms and grows back when it is fast again; stage lists show 2 stages instead of 4; (2) the screen redraws less often (at least every 120 ms, up to once a second when it is struggling) and values that are only displayed are cached for 0.6 s instead of 0.12 s; (3) glows, shadows, filters, animations and transitions are switched off. It changes only how things are DRAWN: production, ticks, offline progress and saves are not touched, and clicking still updates the screen instantly. The character limit box works with or without it: any number from 1 up (0 = never cut), so you can tune it for your device as far as you like.

Factor Boosts

ON gives every Factor Boost you qualify for at once (manual, Refund and automatic). OFF gives exactly 1 per press / per automatic boost.

Factors
